A Fabry-Perot (F-P) etalon, consisting of two high-reflectivity glass plates, is used to analyze light from a Sodium lamp. The etalon's air pressure is tunable, and its transmitivity is given by $T=\frac{1}{1+F \sin ^{2}(\delta / 2)}$, where $F=\frac{4 R}{(1-R)^{2}}$, $\delta=\frac{4 \pi n t \cos \theta}{\lambda}$. The Sodium lamp emits D1 ($\lambda=589.6 \mathrm{~nm}$) and D2 ($\lambda=589 \mathrm{~nm}$) lines. A filter allows only the D1 line to pass through. This light forms circular interference fringes on the focal plane of a lens with focal length $f = 30 \mathrm{~cm}$. The reflectivity of the inner surfaces is $R=90\%$, and the inner-surface spacing is $t=1 \mathrm{~cm}$. The Sodium lamp is placed in a tunable uniform magnetic field.

1. the width $\varepsilon$ of the spectral line.
2. the resolution $\lambda / \Delta \lambda$ of the etalon.
3. As shown in Fig. 1, the initial air pressure is zero. By slowly tuning the pin valve, air is gradually injected into the F-P etalon and finally the air pressure reaches the standard atmospheric pressure. On the same time, ten new fringes are observed to produce from the center of the ring patterns on the focal plane. Based on this phenomenon, calculate the refractive index of air $n_{\text{air}}$ at the standard atmospheric pressure.
4. Energy levels splitting of Sodium atoms occurs when they are placed in a magnetic field. This is called as the Zeeman effect. The energy shift given by $\Delta E=m_{j} g_{k} \mu_{B} B$, where the quantum number $m_{j}$ can be $J, J-1, \ldots, -J+1, -J$, $J$ is the total angular quantum number, $g_{k}$ is the Landé factor, $\mu_{B}=\frac{h e}{4 \pi m_{e}}$ is Bohr magneton, $h$ is the Plank constant, $e$ is the electron charge, $m_{e}$ is the electron mass, $B$ is the magnetic field. As shown in Fig. 3, the D1 spectral line is emitted when Sodium atoms jump from the energy level ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ down to ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$. We have $J=\frac{1}{2}$ for both ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$. Therefore, in the magnetic field, each energy level will be split into two levels. We define the energy gap of two splitting levels as $\Delta E_{1}$ for ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and $\Delta E_{2}$ for ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$ respectively ($\Delta E_{1} < \Delta E_{2}$). As a result, the D1 line is split into 4 spectral lines (a, b, c, and d), as showed in Fig. 3. Please write down the expression of the frequency $(v)$ of four lines $a, b, c$, and $d$.

Figure 3
5. As shown in Fig. 4, when the magnetic field is turned on, each fringe of the D1 line will split into four sub-fringes $(1,2,3$, and $4)$. The diameter of the four sub-fringes near the center is measured as $D_{1}$, $D_{2}$, $D_{3}$, and $D_{4}$. Please give the expression of the splitting energy gap $\Delta E_{1}$ of ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and $\Delta E_{2}$ of ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$.
<img_4460>
Figure 4
6. For the magnetic field $B=0.1 \mathrm{~T}$, the diameter of four sub-fringes is measured as: $D_{1}=3.88 \mathrm{~mm}$, $D_{2}=4.05 \mathrm{~mm}$, $D_{3}=4.35 \mathrm{~mm}$, and $D_{4}=4.51 \mathrm{~mm}$. Please calculate the Landé factor $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{k}1}$ of ${ }^{2} \mathrm{P}_{1/2}$ and $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{k}2}$ of ${ }^{2} \mathrm{S}_{1/2}$.
7. The magnetic field on the sun can be determined by measuring the Zeeman effect of the Sodium D1 line on some special regions of the sun. One observes that, in the four split lines, the wavelength difference between the shortest and longest wavelength is $0.012 \mathrm{~nm}$ by a solar spectrograph. What is the magnetic field $B$ in this region of the sun?
8. A Light- Emitting Diode (LED) source with a central wavelength $\lambda=650 \mathrm{~nm}$ and spectral width $\Delta \lambda=20 \mathrm{~nm}$ is normally incident $(\theta=0)$ into the F-P etalon shown in Fig. 1. For the vacuum case, find (i) the number of lines in transmitted spectrum and (ii) the frequency width $\Delta v$ of each line?

The Etalon consists of two parallel plates, the plate spacing is labeled t, the refractive index of the internal medium is labeled n, and it is connected with a pin valve, Gas in, and piping leading to a vacuum pump. After the emergent light passes through lens L2, it forms concentric circular fringes in front of the microscope on the right side. The upper half of Fig. 4 in the attached figure is labeled B=0, showing the ring cross sections of adjacent orders m and m−1 when not split; the lower half is labeled B≠0, showing each original ring split into four sub-rings labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, and the diameters of the four sub-rings near the center are labeled D1, D2, D3, D4 respectively. The problem also mentions that Fig. 3 is used to label the four spectral lines a, b, c, d, but the details of Fig. 3 are not shown in this attached figure, so below they are only recorded as a, b, c, d according to the four Zeeman components from low frequency to high frequency. Reasoning calculation: R=0.9, so F=4R/(1−R)^2=3.6/0.01=360, sqrt(F)=18.97. Near the transmission maximum let δ=2πm+Δδ, then T=1/[1+F sin^2(Δδ/2)]. At half height T=1/2, therefore F sin^2(Δδ/2)=1; the small-angle approximation gives |Δδ|=2/sqrt(F), so the full width ε=4/sqrt(F)=0.2108 rad≈0.21 rad. Resolving power: the filter only lets the D1 line pass, take λ=589.6 nm. The central order m=2t/λ=2(0.01)/(589.6e−9)=3.392e4. The Fabry-Perot finesse is πsqrt(F)/2=29.80, therefore λ/Δλ=m·πsqrt(F)/2≈3.392e4×29.80=1.01e6. Gas-filled refractive index: at the center cosθ=1, and the central order is 2nt/λ. Each appearance of a new central fringe means that 2nt/λ increases by 1. When gradually filled from vacuum to standard atmospheric pressure, 10 new central fringes appear, therefore 2t(n_air−1)/λ=10, hence n_air=1+10λ/(2t)=1+10(589.6e−9)/0.02=1.0002948≈1.00029. Zeeman frequency: the two branches of the upper energy level 2P1/2 relative to the original energy level are ±ΔE1/2, the two branches of the lower energy level 2S1/2 relative to the original energy level are ±ΔE2/2, and ΔE1<ΔE2. The transition frequency equals the difference between the upper and lower energy levels divided by h. Recording the four components from low frequency to high frequency as a, b, c, d, then va=v0−(ΔE1+ΔE2)/(2h), vb=v0−(ΔE2−ΔE1)/(2h), vc=v0+(ΔE2−ΔE1)/(2h), vd=v0+(ΔE1+ΔE2)/(2h). ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A Fabry-Perot (F-P) etalon, consisting of two high-reflectivity glass plates, is used to analyze light from a Sodium lamp. The etalon's air pressure is tunable, and its transmitivity is given by $T=\frac{1}{1+F \sin ^{2}(\delta / 2)}$, where $F=\frac{4 R}{(1-R)^{2}}$, $\delta=\frac{4 \pi n t \cos \theta}{\lambda}$. The Sodium lamp emits D1 ($\lambda=589.6 \mathrm{~nm}$) and D2 ($\lambda=589 \mathrm{~nm}$) lines. A filter allows only the D1 line to pass through. This light forms circular interference fringes on the focal plane of a lens with focal length $f = 30 \mathrm{~cm}$. The reflectivity of the inner surfaces is $R=90\%$, and the inner-surface spacing is $t=1 \mathrm{~cm}$. The Sodium lamp is placed in a tunable uniform magnetic field. 1. the width $\varepsilon$ of the spectral line. 2. the resolution $\lambda / \Delta \lambda$ of the etalon. 3. As shown in Fig. 1, the initial air pressure is zero. By slowly tuning the pin valve, air is gradually injected into the F-P etalon and finally the air pressure reaches the standard atmospheric pressure. On the same time, ten new fringes are observed to produce from the center of the ring patterns on the focal plane. Based on this phenomenon, calculate the refractive index of air $n_{\text{air}}$ at the standard atmospheric pressure. 4. Energy levels splitting of Sodium atoms occurs when they are placed in a magnetic field. This is called as the Zeeman effect. The energy shift given by $\Delta E=m_{j} g_{k} \mu_{B} B$, where the quantum number $m_{j}$ can be $J, J-1, \ldots, -J+1, -J$, $J$ is the total angular quantum number, $g_{k}$ is the Landé factor, $\mu_{B}=\frac{h e}{4 \pi m_{e}}$ is Bohr magneton, $h$ is the Plank constant, $e$ is the electron charge, $m_{e}$ is the electron mass, $B$ is the magnetic field. As shown in Fig. 3, the D1 spectral line is emitted when Sodium atoms jump from the energy level ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ down to ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$. We have $J=\frac{1}{2}$ for both ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$. Therefore, in the magnetic field, each energy level will be split into two levels. We define the energy gap of two splitting levels as $\Delta E_{1}$ for ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and $\Delta E_{2}$ for ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$ respectively ($\Delta E_{1} < \Delta E_{2}$). As a result, the D1 line is split into 4 spectral lines (a, b, c, and d), as showed in Fig. 3. Please write down the expression of the frequency $(v)$ of four lines $a, b, c$, and $d$. Figure 3 5. As shown in Fig. 4, when the magnetic field is turned on, each fringe of the D1 line will split into four sub-fringes $(1,2,3$, and $4)$. The diameter of the four sub-fringes near the center is measured as $D_{1}$, $D_{2}$, $D_{3}$, and $D_{4}$. Please give the expression of the splitting energy gap $\Delta E_{1}$ of ${ }^{2} P_{1 / 2}$ and $\Delta E_{2}$ of ${ }^{2} S_{1 / 2}$. Figure 4 6. For the magnetic field $B=0.1 \mathrm{~T}$, the diameter of four sub-fringes is measured as: $D_{1}=3.88 \mathrm{~mm}$, $D_{2}=4.05 \mathrm{~mm}$, $D_{3}=4.35 \mathrm{~mm}$, and $D_{4}=4.51 \mathrm{~mm}$. Please calculate the Landé factor $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{k}1}$ of ${ }^{2} \mathrm{P}_{1/2}$ and $\mathrm{g}_{\mathrm{k}2}$ of ${ }^{2} \mathrm{S}_{1/2}$. 7. The magnetic field on the sun can be determined by measuring the Zeeman effect of the Sodium D1 line on some special regions of the sun. One observes that, in the four split lines, the wavelength difference between the shortest and longest wavelength is $0.012 \mathrm{~nm}$ by a solar spectrograph. What is the magnetic field $B$ in this region of the sun? 8. A Light- Emitting Diode (LED) source with a central wavelength $\lambda=650 \mathrm{~nm}$ and spectral width $\Delta \lambda=20 \mathrm{~nm}$ is normally incident $(\theta=0)$ into the F-P etalon shown in Fig. 1. For the vacuum case, find (i) the number of lines in transmitted spectrum and (ii) the frequency width $\Delta v$ of each line?
